title: The Stories Families Keep
sentences: Every family quietly agrees on a version of its own history, however loosely it fits the facts.
One sibling is remembered as difficult, another as dependable, and the roles rarely get revised.
These stories are comforting precisely because they spare everyone the effort of reconsidering.
Duty, too, gets distributed early and unevenly, and it calcifies long before anyone notices.
The child who stayed nearby absorbs an obligation that the one who left is rarely asked to share.
Resentment, when it surfaces, is often less about the present than about an old, unspoken ledger.
And yet naming that ledger aloud can feel like betrayal, as though love required silence.
Arguably, families endure not by resolving these tensions but by learning to work around them.
To the extent that a shared story keeps the peace, its accuracy becomes almost beside the point.
What outsiders see as harmony may simply be old grievances that nobody has the energy to reopen.
